collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and two healers or two other adults; in the story (name1) has a long-term joint illness)

collection.description: Two healers disagree about a villager's aching joints and wait outside for a decision: try both, or ask for time to think.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s joints ache, and they have for years. It's an illness that comes and goes. Two healers have looked at (subject.him/her) this week and disagree completely. One says rest, warm compresses and gentle movement. The other says a bitter root tea that some people swear by. Both of them are waiting outside (subject.his/her) hut for (subject.him/her) to decide. (friend) is one of them.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) tries both, and keeps careful track. The warm compresses help on bad days. The tea helps a little, maybe, but tastes like mud and gives (subject.him/her) a stomach ache. (subject.He/she) keeps the compresses and the gentle walking and quietly stops the tea. (subject.He/she) tells both healers exactly what (subject.he/she) found. They argue about it. (subject) leaves them to it.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) asks both of them to leave, please, and let (subject.him/her) think. (subject.He/she) asks friends, asks an elder with the same aches, and thinks for a few days. Then (subject.he/she) chooses: the compresses and the movement, no tea. The tea healer is a little offended. "It's my body," (subject) says, "and I know how it feels better than anyone." (subject.He/she) isn't cured. (subject.He/she) does feel a little better.
